rows.estimation_basis: Estimates are strictly based on historical data from the Fleet Tracking Portal for a Logistics Operator project (id=001-logistics-fleet-portal, total 3,400 hours over 20 weeks). Scope has been adjusted down from three telematics vendors to two (reducing integration effort from 520h to 360-440h). The asset count (300 service vans vs. 600 trucks) reduces the load profiling and clustering complexity, lowering map and alert tuning efforts slightly while preserving critical spatial processing and WebSocket pipelines. Driver CRUD, auth, and reporting mirror the reference project with adjustments for the specific weekly KPI definitions. QA, DevOps, and stabilization remain significant components (totaling ~760-940h) to incorporate rigorous testing of real-time ingest reliability and vendor failure modes identified in past lessons learned.

No reference projects were provided in the RFP. All estimates are derived bottom-up based on standard enterprise engineering metrics for distributed IoT ingestion, geospatial processing, and reactive UI development. The breakdown explicitly accounts for the full delivery lifecycle including discovery, multi-vendor integration, automated testing, geospatial edge-case handling, DevOps pipelines, and stabilization.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project 002-fintech-kyc-onboarding (KYC Onboarding Platform for a Digital Bank; total 5,200 hours, 26 weeks). The requirements align closely across all functional domains: customer onboarding wizard (ref: 480h vs proposed: 440-520h), identity vendor integration (ref: 460h vs proposed: 420-500h), sanctions/PEP screening (ref: 340h vs proposed: 320-380h), rules engine (ref: 560h vs proposed: 520-600h), compliance console with audit trail (ref: 720h vs proposed: 680-780h), GDPR/PII security (ref: 420h vs proposed: 380-460h), admin/reporting (ref: 380h vs proposed: 340-420h), infrastructure/hardening (ref: 640h vs proposed: 580-680h), and regulatory QA/sign-off support (ref: 1,200h vs proposed: 1,100-1,300h). Risk mitigations directly incorporate lessons learned regarding sandbox behavioral divergence and mid-flight regulatory scope expansion.

No reference projects were provided in the brief. Estimates are built bottom-up from general engineering experience delivering fintech and regulated onboarding solutions. Effort includes end-to-end human delivery across discovery, architecture, UI/UX implementation, third-party vendor integration, back-office dashboard development, automated testing, security reviews, and deployment stabilization. A baseline uncertainty factor of 20-25% is incorporated to accommodate external vendor API variations and evolving compliance specifications.

Estimates are strictly derived from historical delivery data from the reference project 'B2B Marketplace for Industrial Parts' (id=003-ecommerce-b2b-marketplace, 6,100 total hours, 30 weeks duration). We reused the benchmark hours for core modules: Catalogue Import Pipeline (~620h baseline), Search & Filtering (~540h baseline), Customer-Specific Pricing & RFQ Workflow (~780h baseline), Stripe Connect Split Payments (~700h baseline), Supplier Portal (~820h baseline), Admin Back-Office (~520h baseline), Angular SSR (~340h baseline), DevOps (~380h baseline), and QA/UAT (~920h baseline). We adjusted the scope by removing the Buyer Punch-Out (cXML/OCI) module (480h in reference) as it was not requested in the brief, resulting in a project baseline of approximately 5,190 to 5,940 total engineering hours across a 26-week timeline with parallel delivery tracks.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project 004-healthcare-patient-app (Patient Appointment and Telehealth App: 3,900 total hours across 22 weeks), which covered Flutter mobile delivery, FastAPI services, Twilio video, and HIPAA audit controls. Hours for appointment scheduling (480-560h), video teleconsultation (360-420h), notifications (380-440h), and the web dashboard (520-600h) closely mirror the reference implementation. The custom HL7 FHIR integration effort from the reference was reallocated toward dental-specific scheduling rules, multi-chair operatory management, and cloud DevOps hardening, yielding an aligned aggregate delivery scope of 3,070 to 3,600 engineering hours.

Estimates are directly grounded in historical data from reference project 'Internal HR Knowledge Assistant (RAG)' (id=005-hr-internal-ai-assistant, 1,500 total hours, 10 weeks). Core modules (Document ingestion 240h, Retrieval 200h, Chat UI 260h, Access control 180h, SSO/Deployment 140h, and QA/UAT 240h) mirror the proven architecture of Angular + FastAPI + Qdrant. Scope adjustments were applied to reflect legal domain complexities: document volume increases from 400 HR files to 800+ legal precedents and memos with complex layouts and cross-citations (+40h ingestion), and evaluation/observability were expanded from 240h (160h eval + 80h monitoring) to 220h-260h to incorporate comprehensive legal evaluation benchmarks, hallucination guards, and strict audit compliance. Total delivery timeline is projected at 11 weeks for a balanced engineering team.

Estimates are derived directly from Reference Project 008 (Offline-First Field Service App for Technicians), which totaled 3,600 delivery hours across 21 weeks using an identical architectural paradigm (Ionic Angular, NestJS, SQLite, and ERP connectivity). Historical data from 008 established that the offline sync engine and conflict resolution required 760 hours and was the largest source of defect risk; consequently, the offline engine is allocated 700-840 hours (accounting for a 20-25% variance buffer for edge cases). Field forms, checklists, and photo/signature capture closely match reference allocations (520h and 300h) with adjustments for HVAC-specific dynamic inspection logic. ERP synchronization (520h in ref) is budgeted at 480-580 hours to accommodate parts inventory ledger synchronization. Cross-cutting delivery activities, including DevOps, physical device lab testing, and an extensive field pilot, reflect proven historical proportions to guarantee operational stability.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project 002-fintech-kyc-onboarding (KYC Onboarding Platform for a Digital Bank, total 5,200 hours, 26 weeks), which shares a near-identical architectural topology: document intake, external ID verification vendor webhooks, risk scoring rules, human review consoles, KMS/PII encryption, and strict audit logs. We adjusted hours per module: document intake (440-520h vs 480h reference) allows for photo/document uploads; identity vendor integration (420-500h vs 460h reference); rules engine (520-620h vs 560h reference); adjuster review console (680-780h vs 720h reference); PII and encryption (400-480h vs 420h reference); and admin/reporting (340-420h vs 380h reference). We excluded dedicated sanctions screening (340h from reference) as it was not specified in the insurance intake brief. QA, compliance verification, and infrastructure hardening reflect reference project lessons learned to absorb compliance-driven adjustments and vendor testing contingencies.

Estimates are strictly derived from two past reference projects: 'Offline-First Field Service App for Technicians' (008-mobile-field-service: 3,600 hrs) and 'Fleet Tracking Portal for a Logistics Operator' (001-logistics-fleet-portal: 3,400 hrs). Estimates are grounded in historical metrics from two delivered reference projects: 'Learning Management System for Corporate Training' (id=007-edtech-lms, 2,800 hours) and 'Internal HR Knowledge Assistant (RAG)' (id=005-hr-internal-ai-assistant, 1,500 hours). From 007-edtech-lms, we extracted core LMS domains: User Management/SSO (adjusted from 220h to 180-220h for university SSO), Course Authoring (adjusted from 480h to 380-460h), Video Delivery & Progress (280-340h, matching the 300h baseline), Quizzes & Assessments (320-380h, aligning with 340h historical effort), and Certification (isolated to 160-200h). Corporate-specific SCORM packaging (420h) was deliberately excluded as it was not specified. From 005-hr-internal-ai-assistant, we synthesized the AI RAG components: Chunking & Ingestion (220-260h vs 240h ref), Hybrid Retrieval & Reranking (200-240h vs 200h ref), Chat UI with Citation Streaming (240-280h vs 260h ref), and Guardrails/Evaluation/Monitoring (combined 280-360h reflecting historical 160h eval + 80h monitoring + 180h access control). Comprehensive DevOps, QA, and UAT are mapped proportionally at 600-740h across the expanded joint surface area, producing a realistic total baseline delivery effort spanning 22 calendar weeks with parallel work streams.
